bottleneck: Early intervention can rewire developing brains, but most neurodevelopmental disorders are diagnosed after critical plasticity windows have narrowed: autism is typically identified at age 3-4, dyslexia after reading failure, ADHD after school struggles. No reliable infant biomarkers predict these conditions before symptoms emerge, and the timing, duration, and limits of human critical periods are poorly mapped — we know the windows exist without knowing their schedules. Medicine arrives after the brain's most plastic phase has passed, when interventions must work against consolidated circuits rather than with developing ones.
current_state: Early behavioral screening is improving, but biology-based prediction in infancy does not exist for most conditions, and critical-period timing in humans is inferred from animals.

sources.title: Brain Connectome: Mapping Neural Networks in Neuroscience

title: Neurodevelopmental disorders diagnosed after plasticity windows
why_it_blocks: The developing brain is the most treatable brain, yet diagnosis lags behind plasticity by years. Closing the timing gap would multiply every intervention's power — early action on a plastic brain beats late action on a fixed one.
